attempts.entry_title: Human GABAergic interneurons in acute and cultured slices (Lee, Dalley et al. 2023)
attempts.summary: Much of this Patch-seq study of human interneurons holds: subclasses differ in sag and spike shape, SST FRZB neurons resemble PVALB neurons, and human and mouse homologues differ in sag, rheobase and spike width. Not reproduced were the electrophysiological overlap of cultured and acute PVALB WFDC2 neurons, the intermingling of double bouquet cells with other SST cells, and the species separation of Sst 5 cells. Gene differences between SST CALB1 morphology types came to 2, not 253, suggesting the Methods do not describe the procedure run. The culture effect on sag and spike width could not be decided, as the paper does not name its sweeps, and the transcriptomic comparisons need a Seurat integration the agent could not run.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Lee, Dalley et al. (2023) on dandiset 000636, which holds the Patch-seq electrophysiology of 706 human cortical GABAergic neurons from acute and cultured slices. Features are computed from the NWB files with IPFX and labelled through the paper's code repository, which also supplies the transcriptomes and morphology features used for the claims whose data are not in the dandiset. The comparison with mouse uses the recordings of dandiset 000020.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Lee, Dalley et al. (2023) from dandiset 000636
Human against mouse, dandisets 000636 and 000020 (Lee, Dalley et al. 2023)

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's NWB files can be matched to the paper's per-cell metadata and feature tables in its code repository, and features recomputed from the files agree with those tables.
outcomes.source: Data and materials availability; github.com/AllenInstitute/human_patchseq_gaba commit 5eb357a, data/README.md, LeeDalley_manuscript_metadata_v2.csv and LeeDalley_ephys_fx.csv
outcomes.notes: Files are matched to metadata rows by nwb_id, which equals the NWB session id. 684 of the 704 unique rows with Has_ephys (97.2%) have a file; 14 of these rows have no nwb_id and 6 have one that is not in the dandiset. 16 files have no metadata row, and 6 rows without Has_ephys have a file. Of the cells with values on both sides, rheobase_i agrees within 10% for 92.2% (650 cells), input_resistance 94.5%, sag 97.8% and width_rheo 98.8% (586 cells); the median relative difference is 0 for all four. All four agree together for 90.6% of 586 cells, a stricter reading shown only. Over the 65 features computed, a median of 93.6% of cells agree within 10%. Nine features agree for less than 80% of cells (fi_fit_slope 41%, isi_cv_mean 46%, adapt_mean 58%, isi_norm_sq_var_mean 60%, isi_norm_sq_var_max 71%, adapt_max 77%, isi_adapt_ratio 27%, and upstroke_ramp and threshold_i_ramp just under 80%). For the first seven the definitions here (assumptions in the helper) are not the paper's.
deviations: The criterion is read per feature (each of the four features within 10% for at least 90% of the cells with both values), as "the cells with both values" suggests; the joint reading (90.6%) also passes.
Cell-level QC (seal and access resistance) is not recomputed; the Methods' sweep QC is applied (bridge balance, bias current, noise), which may explain part of the rheobase disagreement.

outcomes.statement: The study characterized 778 human GABAergic neurons in layers 2 to 6, covering 44 of the 45 GABAergic t-types, with electrophysiology from 75 LAMP5/PAX6, 99 VIP, 149 SST and 352 PVALB neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, Comparison of features across human GABAergic subclasses, paragraphs 1 and 3
outcomes.quote: properties of 778 neurons from the four canonical GABAergic subclasses in human cortex. We described neurons in cortical layers 2 to 6 (L2–6) across 44 transcriptomic types ... LAMP5/PAX6 ( n = 75), VIP ( n = 99), SST ( n = 149), and PVALB ( n = 352)
outcomes.notes: The metadata table holds 778 unique neurons in 44 t-types, as the paper says. Over the 686 labelled files with a QC-passing long square sweep, reading (a), Revised_subclass_label, gives LAMP5/PAX6 64, VIP 101, SST 158 and PVALB 363; three are within tolerance and LAMP5/PAX6 is not (64 against 75, tolerance 7.5). Reading (b), subclass_label, gives 69, 96, 231 and 290, two within tolerance. The 675 cells with a rheobase computed here equal the paper's total (75 + 99 + 149 + 352), but split 63, 99, 155 and 358. All 704 rows with Has_ephys give 67, 111, 156 and 370 under reading (a), so the paper's 75 LAMP5/PAX6 cannot be counted from its own table either. The metadata table lists layers 1 and 5_6 for some cells as well as 2 to 6.
deviations: Cell-level inclusion criteria (seal, access resistance) are not recomputed from the test pulses; a cell counts when it has at least one long square sweep passing the Methods' sweep QC.

outcomes.statement: Patch-seq neurons from slices in culture (2 to 16 days) had more genes detected than neurons from acute slices.
outcomes.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 1; Figure 1B
outcomes.quote: Patch-seq neurons from culture preparations recorded at 2 to 16 days in culture (DIC) had significantly ( P < 0.0001) higher genes detected as compared with the acute paradigm
outcomes.notes: On the Genes_Detected column, which the code's notebook plots as Genes.Detected of metaPatch (equal for all 778 cells), culture median 7318 (n = 467) against acute 6802 (n = 311), two-sided Mann-Whitney p = 1.6e-05. On genes above 0 in the expression matrix, a variant, 12203 against 11259, p = 4.3e-10. Both are below p = 0.0001.
deviations: The matrix count of genes above 0 does not equal the Genes_Detected column for any cell (median difference 4394 genes). The column is used, as the code's notebook plots it; the matrix count is shown as a variant, and the test holds for both.
outcomes.where: GitHub AllenInstitute/human_patchseq_gaba commit 5eb357a, data/complete_patchseq_data_sets1.RData and complete_patchseq_data_sets2.RData (Genes_Detected also in LeeDalley_manuscript_metadata_v2.csv)

outcomes.statement: Culture neurons fall into two clusters, with and without a microglial gene signature, and the signature is also present, less strongly, in a subset of acute neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 1; fig. S1B and S1C
outcomes.quote: These neurons clustered into two domains, with or without microglial gene expression signatures ... This microglial signature ( data S2 ) was also observed in a subset of neurons collected with the acute paradigm, although the effect was less pronounced
outcomes.notes: The criterion's two readings of "less pronounced" give different outcomes, and the criterion blocks the claim in that case. The code's Seurat clustering is run with a Python substitute (vst variable genes, scaling, 20 PCs, a UMAP with Seurat's defaults, a shared-neighbour graph on the UMAP and Louvain at the code's resolutions). At resolution 0.001 the 467 culture cells form two clusters under four of the five seeds, the claim's among them, and three under seed +3000 (the third splits the cells without the signature); the microglial cluster has 171 to 173 cells with mean expression of the 269 Data S2 genes 6.0 against 1.1 (Mann-Whitney p 1.1e-72 to 2.8e-72). The calls at resolution 0.1 agree with condition2 for 96.7% to 98.2% of cells. Reading (b) holds, the acute microglial cells express the genes less (mean 3.6 to 3.8 against 5.9). Reading (a) fails, a larger fraction of acute than culture cells is called microglial (0.40 to 0.47 against 0.38); the paper's own calls give the same (0.418 against 0.385).
deviations: Seurat cannot be installed in the entry's locked Python environment, so its steps are run in Python with Seurat's default parameters (vst with a lowess for loess, uwot's defaults in umap-learn, Louvain of networkx with one start). The microglial genes for the second step are the 269 of Data S2 marked used_for_defining_microglial_signature, the set the code's culture_DEX step produced, not recomputed.
outcomes.where: GitHub AllenInstitute/human_patchseq_gaba commit 5eb357a, data/complete_patchseq_data_sets1.RData and complete_patchseq_data_sets2.RData

outcomes.statement: For the top differentially expressed genes of each GABAergic subclass, average expression in acute and culture neurons is strongly correlated.
outcomes.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 1; Figure 1C
outcomes.quote: Upon examination of key differentially expressed genes responsible for GABAergic subclass discrimination, average gene expression was strongly correlated ( P < 0.0001), demonstrating alignment between acute and culture paradigms

statistics.test: correlation, test not named (Fig. 1C legend gives a regression line)
statistics.n: top 25 differentially expressed genes per subclass

outcomes.notes: Every reading run holds. Per subclass, Pearson r is 0.81 to 0.95 on log2(CPM + 1) and 0.82 to 0.97 on CPM, Spearman 0.75 to 0.94, all p < 1e-4 with 25 genes; pooled over 100 genes, r = 0.87 to 0.92. Cells per subclass, acute and culture, are 57 and 25 (LAMP5/PAX6), 145 and 258 (PVALB), 30 and 141 (SST), 79 and 43 (VIP).
deviations: The genes are the 25 with the largest difference in mean log2(CPM + 1) between a subclass's Patch-seq cells and the other cells, a standard choice. The criterion's other reading, the snRNA-seq ranking, could not be run, as the code repository does not hold the dissociated nuclei data its notebook loads (complete_facs_data_sets.RData). The outcome rests on the Patch-seq readings, an assumption.
outcomes.where: GitHub AllenInstitute/human_patchseq_gaba commit 5eb357a, data/complete_patchseq_data_sets1.RData and complete_patchseq_data_sets2.RData

outcomes.notes: marker_sum_norm_label, acute median 0.962 (n = 311) and culture 0.962 (n = 467), two-sided Mann-Whitney p = 0.38, rank-biserial -0.037.

outcomes.statement: Fifty morphological features of depth-matched PVALB WFDC2 neurons do not differ between culture (n = 9) and acute (n = 10) slices.
outcomes.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 2; Figure 1G; fig. S2A
outcomes.quote: We also evaluated 50 morphological features of cortical depth–matched PVALB WFDC2 neurons ( Fig. 1F ) from culture ( n = 9) and acute paradigms ( n = 10) and didn’t find any difference among the two conditions

statistics.n: 9 culture and 10 acute PVALB WFDC2 neurons

outcomes.notes: The feature table has 16 acute and 10 culture PVALB WFDC2 reconstructions, not the paper's 10 and 9. No feature differs at FDR p < 0.05 under any reading. (a) All 26 cells, smallest FDR p 0.117 (smallest raw p 0.0029, soma_surface). (b) The 9 and 9 cells inside the depth range both groups share, smallest FDR p 0.202. (c) Each culture cell with its nearest-depth acute cell, 10 and 10, smallest FDR p 0.090. Culture somas are shallower (median 535 against 837 um).

The 50 features are the table's 51 columns less soma depth, which the matching uses. How the paper depth-matched its 9 and 10 cells is not given; two matchings were run, and all readings give the same outcome.

outcomes.statement: In PVALB WFDC2 neurons, 43 of 84 electrophysiological features differ between the acute and culture paradigms.
outcomes.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 2; fig. S2B; preprint, same section
outcomes.quote: Analysis of electrophysiological responses from PVALB WFDC2 neurons revealed that 43 of 84 features differed across the two paradigms
outcomes.notes: 19 of the 84 features (width_suprathresh, postap_slope, sag_area, sag_peak_t, sag_tau, sag_depol, ahp_delay_ratio, trough_slowdeltav and adp_v_last features) are not computed by public IPFX; the Methods say "custom code used for chirps and some high-level features will be released in a future version of IPFX". Over the 65 features computed, 41 differ between 65 acute and 82 culture PVALB WFDC2 cells at BH-FDR p < 0.05 (63%, the paper 51%). Counting the 19 missing features as all non-significant or all significant bounds the count over 84 between 39 and 61, which contains the whole tolerance (38.7 to 47.3), so the outcome cannot be decided. As variants, the paper's own table gives 47 of 84 for the same cells (53 of 93), and the computed features with the paper's values for the missing 19 give 50. With culture restricted to cells without (with) the microglial signature, 37 (30) of 65 differ.

outcomes.statement: In PVALB WFDC2 neurons AP width and sag differ between acute and culture slices (sag is higher in culture), while interspike interval and input resistance do not.
outcomes.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 2; Figure 1L; preprint Discussion, paragraph 2 (direction of sag)
outcomes.quote: AP width and sag are two of the key features that were different between the two groups ( Fig. 1L ); however, multiple other cardinal intrinsic membrane properties, such as interspike interval or input resistance, were not

statistics.about: AP width and sag, acute against culture

outcomes.notes: The readings give different outcomes, so the claim is blocked as its criterion says. Sag is higher in culture (median 0.284 against 0.110, FDR p = 1.2e-14). AP width is wider in culture at FDR p < 1e-4 for the rheobase (FDR p = 5.6e-05), hero (6.6e-06) and short square (7.7e-05) sweeps; the ramp gives FDR p = 0.0077. Input resistance does not differ (FDR p = 0.81). The ISI of the hero sweep does not differ (FDR p = 0.75), but that of the rheobase sweep does (FDR p = 0.016, 74 cells with two or more spikes at rheobase). Five of the eight readings fail (the four with the rheobase ISI, and the ramp width with the hero ISI); under the hero ISI with rheobase, hero or short square width the claim holds. All 10 PVALB WFDC2 files at 200 kHz are culture cells; over the 50 kHz files only, width differs at FDR p 4.4e-06 to 3.6e-05 for the same three sweeps, so the sampling rate does not explain the width difference. With BH over 84 features and the 19 missing ones at p = 1, the largest FDR p width_short_square can have is 9.9e-05. Open question for the authors, which sweep's ISI and width Fig. 1L plots.
deviations: BH-FDR across the 65 computed features, as the 84 cannot all be computed; the bound over 84 is shown.

outcomes.statement: The features that differ in culture already differ at 2 days in culture and do not change with further days in culture.
outcomes.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 2; fig. S2C (preprint Supplementary Figure 2C, sag and AP width against days in culture)
outcomes.quote: The features that were different between the two paradigms were observed at the earliest time point (2 DIC) and did not change with additional days in culture
outcomes.notes: It depends on fig1l-width-sag-differ, which is blocked, and its own width readings disagree. Over 82 culture PVALB WFDC2 cells, sag does not correlate with days in culture (r = 0.07, FDR p 0.51 to 0.70). Width does not for the rheobase, hero and ramp sweeps (r -0.05 to 0.08) but does for the short square (r = 0.37, FDR p = 0.0015). The one 2 DIC PVALB WFDC2 cell has sag 0.379 and width 0.54 to 0.61 ms, above the acute medians (0.110, 0.41 to 0.49 ms) as the culture group is. Of the 41 features that differ, 4 correlate with days in culture at BH p < 0.05.

outcomes.statement: In electrophysiology UMAP space of all 84 features, acute and culture PVALB WFDC2 neurons occupy a similar space.
outcomes.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 2; Figure 1I
outcomes.quote: When projecting all 84 electrophysiological features through the UMAP, PVALB WFDC2 neurons from both paradigms occupied a similar space
outcomes.notes: In feature space, culture PVALB WFDC2 cells have a mean of 0.191 acute cells among their 15 nearest PVALB WFDC2 neighbours, against a shuffle median of 0.446 (ratio 0.43, under the criterion's 0.5); acute cells 0.408 against 0.563 (0.72). In the UMAP embedding the ratios are 0.68 to 0.82 under all five seeds, which passes. With 10 and 30 neighbours the feature-space culture ratio is 0.36 and 0.48. The feature-space result does not depend on the seed beyond the shuffle (0.43 under all five). With the paper's values for the 19 missing features added, the feature-space culture ratio is 0.45, so the missing features do not explain the failure. On the paper's own table of all 84 features it is 0.51, which passes narrowly, so the result depends on how the 65 shared features are computed (nine of them agree with the paper's table for fewer than 80% of cells, cell-metadata-link).
deviations: The 65 computed features in place of 84; the paper's table is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: Of 114 voltage-gated ion-channel genes, only seven differ in expression between culture and acute neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 3; fig. S2D; Discussion, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: We examined 114 voltage-gated ion-channel genes and found only seven that were different in culture versus acute paradigm
outcomes.notes: The code's linear model (condition + isImmune + interaction, then apply(lm_pval, 2, p.adjust)) was run on 168 PVALB WFDC2 transcriptomes and the 40551 genes with mean > 0.01. The notebook prints the code's chunk; lm_pval is built by apply over the genes, so it has the three model terms as rows and the genes as columns, and apply(lm_pval, 2, p.adjust) adjusts each gene's three term p-values with Holm. The code also keeps only its keepGenes, which it builds from the dissociated-nuclei data (complete_facs_data_sets.RData) and sex and mitochondrial gene lists, none of which is in the repository. Without that filter 142 channel genes are tested, against the paper's 114, so the procedure is not the paper's; 22 of them have adjusted p <= 0.01 (Holm across genes 1, BH across genes 12, unadjusted 34). The count is not judged against 7. The dissociated-nuclei data are on the Allen portal without a pinned version. Which adjustment the criterion means is asked of a reader (questions/lee-2023.yaml).
outcomes.where: GitHub AllenInstitute/human_patchseq_gaba commit 5eb357a, data/complete_patchseq_data_sets1.RData, complete_patchseq_data_sets2.RData and vgic_genes.csv

outcomes.statement: The four GABAergic subclasses are separable in electrophysiology feature space, with PVALB neurons occupying the most distinct region.
outcomes.source: Results, Comparison of features across human GABAergic subclasses, paragraph 1; Figure 2B
outcomes.quote: PVALB, SST, VIP, and LAMP5/PAX6 interneurons were separable when visualized by electrophysiological ( Fig. 2B ) and morphological ( Fig. 2C ) features in UMAP space, with PVALB neurons occupying the most distinct subregions in both UMAPs
outcomes.notes: PVALB has the highest same-subclass fraction among 15 neighbours in every space and seed (0.844 in feature space, 0.876 to 0.880 in UMAP). In feature space the VIP fraction (0.342) exceeds its share (0.147) by 0.195, under the criterion's 0.2; the other three exceed by 0.22 to 0.34. In UMAP all four exceed 0.2 under the claim's seed (smallest SST 0.202) and three other seeds, and SST misses under +1000 (0.200, under 0.2 before rounding). The feature space fails under every seed. With the paper's values for the 19 missing features added, all four exceed 0.2 in both spaces (smallest excess 0.222 in both), and on the paper's own 84-feature table as well (0.211 and 0.256), so the failing part rests on the 19 features public IPFX does not compute. The criterion asks for the 84 features and only 65 can be computed from the dataset, so the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified, as figs2b-wfdc2-ephys-43-of-84 is for the same 19 features (agreed in the third verification round). UMAP numbers differ between machines under the same seed; in the executed copy the third verifier reviewed, the smallest UMAP excess under the claim's seed was 0.209, SST missed under +1000 and +4000 (0.197, 0.199), and the UMAP with the 19 features added gave 0.224. 686 cells, PVALB 363, SST 158, VIP 101, LAMP5/PAX6 64. The four non-positive values set missing (round 2) moved the VIP excess from 0.193 to 0.195.
deviations: The 65 computed features in place of 84; the paper's table is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: The four subclasses are separable in morphological feature space, PVALB the most distinct.
outcomes.source: Results, Comparison of features across human GABAergic subclasses, paragraph 1; Figure 2C
outcomes.quote: PVALB, SST, VIP, and LAMP5/PAX6 interneurons were separable when visualized by electrophysiological ( Fig. 2B ) and morphological ( Fig. 2C ) features in UMAP space
outcomes.notes: Over 140 reconstructions, PVALB has the highest same-subclass fraction in both spaces and every seed (0.78 in feature space, 0.72 to 0.75 in UMAP). In feature space LAMP5/PAX6 (13 cells) exceed their share by 0.10 and VIP by 0.19, under 0.2. In UMAP SST exceeds by 0.175 under the claim's seed and 0.137 to 0.213 over the five seeds; all four pass under one seed (+2000). The feature space fails under every seed. The PVALB part holds and the separability part holds for two of the four subclasses in feature space.
deviations: Tested on the paper's morphology feature table, all 51 columns, z-scored.
outcomes.where: Brain Image Library doi:10.35077/g.892; GitHub AllenInstitute/human_patchseq_gaba commit 5eb357a, data/LeeDalley_morpho_features.csv

outcomes.statement: LAMP5/PAX6 neurons have the shortest soma-to-branch-tip Euclidean distance for both axon and dendrite.
outcomes.source: Results, Comparison of features across human GABAergic subclasses, paragraph 2; Figure 2E
outcomes.quote: They also had the shortest soma–to–branch tip Euclidean distance for both axon and dendrite

statistics.test: Kruskal-Wallis ANOVA on ranks, post-hoc Dunn's test

outcomes.notes: LAMP5/PAX6 (13 cells) have the lowest median axon_max_euclidean_distance (434 um; PVALB 639, VIP 707, SST 920) and basal_dendrite_max_euclidean_distance (171 um; SST 300, VIP 345, PVALB 348). Kruskal-Wallis p = 4.6e-06 and 2.4e-04. Dunn's FDR p of LAMP5/PAX6 against the others is 1.6e-06 to 7.9e-04 for the axon, and 3.5e-04 to 0.053 for the dendrite (SST 0.053).

outcomes.where: Brain Image Library doi:10.35077/g.892; GitHub AllenInstitute/human_patchseq_gaba commit 5eb357a, data/LeeDalley_morpho_features.csv

outcomes.statement: APs of the PVALB subclass have the fastest kinetics, and LAMP5/PAX6 APs have the highest peak amplitude of the four subclasses.
outcomes.source: Results, Comparison of features across human GABAergic subclasses, paragraph 3; Figure 2F
outcomes.quote: APs from PVALB subclass had the fastest kinetics, whereas LAMP5/PAX6 had the highest peak amplitude versus other subclasses
outcomes.notes: Both readings agree. PVALB has the narrowest AP (short square median 0.48 ms against 0.66 to 0.74; rheobase 0.52 against 0.74 to 0.80) and the lowest upstroke/downstroke ratio (1.81 against 2.25 to 2.38; 1.68 against 2.32 to 2.52), with Dunn's FDR p <= 7.1e-14 against every subclass. LAMP5/PAX6 has the highest median peak (71.9 mV short square, 70.6 mV rheobase), but not significantly against all others, VIP p = 0.08 for the short square and SST p = 0.061 for the rheobase sweep, so the peak part fails the criterion. The kinetics part holds and the peak part holds by medians only.

outcomes.statement: LAMP5/PAX6 and VIP neurons have minimal sag compared with PVALB and SST neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, Comparison of features across human GABAergic subclasses, paragraph 3; Figure 2G
outcomes.quote: LAMP5/PAX6 and VIP subclasses had minimal sag compared with PVALB and SST subclasses
outcomes.notes: Median sag LAMP5/PAX6 0.100 and VIP 0.153 against PVALB 0.241 and SST 0.300; the four pairs differ at Dunn's FDR p 8.7e-13 to 1.9e-06; Kruskal-Wallis p = 8.1e-18. The pooled result mixes conditions, as the criterion and the paper pool them. Sag is higher in culture and most LAMP5/PAX6 (39 of 63) and VIP (57 of 99) cells are acute, while most SST cells are culture (136 of 155). Within acute cells VIP (0.167) has higher sag than PVALB (0.106, Dunn p = 0.0048) and does not differ from SST (0.251, p = 0.20); within culture cells LAMP5/PAX6 (0.256) does not differ from PVALB (0.283, p = 0.40) or SST (0.303, p = 0.31).

outcomes.statement: Several additional electrophysiological features differ between the subclasses.
outcomes.source: Results, Comparison of features across human GABAergic subclasses, paragraph 3; Figure 2H
outcomes.quote: Several additional features further demonstrated the electrophysiological distinctness of each subclass

statistics.test: Kruskal-Wallis ANOVA on ranks, post-hoc Dunn's test

outcomes.notes: 59 of 65 features differ across subclasses at BH-FDR p < 0.05 (Kruskal-Wallis); 44 are outside width, upstroke/downstroke ratio, peak and sag, and 43 of these have a Dunn pair at p < 0.05. The strongest are tau, downstroke and input resistance.

outcomes.statement: Most SST FRZB neurons colocalize with the PVALB subclass in electrophysiology space.
outcomes.source: Results, Revising subclass assignment based on multimodal data, paragraph 2; Figure 3C
outcomes.quote: Examination of all 84 electrophysiological features, visualized using a UMAP, revealed that most of the SST FRZB neurons colocalized with the PVALB subclass
outcomes.notes: With features z-scored over the SST and PVALB cells, as the criterion says, 72 of 73 SST FRZB cells have a PVALB majority among their 15 nearest SST or PVALB neighbours in feature space, and 70 to 72 in UMAP over the five seeds. The criterion's threshold is below chance. findings.statement: The NWB files hold no cell type, subclass, brain region, cortical layer, slice condition (acute or culture), days in culture or virus; their electrode location is empty. Every label the paper's analyses need comes from the code repository's metadata table, linked by its nwb_id column.

16 of the 706 files have no row in the paper's metadata table (sessions 567737666, 567773605, 569870997, 571674350, 591326867, 591342850, 595591210, 595597605, 595715586, 601916346, 611610562, 611822740, 611901143, 847874997, 847908770, 855354224), so they cannot be labelled. 20 metadata rows with Has_ephys have no file (14 without nwb_id, 6 whose nwb_id is not in the dandiset).
The dandiset's assetsSummary gives numberOfCells 616, but the version holds 706 files of one cell each.
79 files have sweeps sampled at 200 kHz (all recorded in 2020 and 2021), where the Methods state that data were digitized at 50 kHz; two files mix rates (25 and 50 kHz, 50 and 200 kHz).
The subject species is written "Homo Sapiens" in 581 files and "Homo sapiens" in 125.

The code repository's Genes_Detected column does not equal the number of genes above 0 in its own expression matrices for any of the 778 cells (median difference 4394 genes), and no threshold from 0 to 5 on the stored log2(CPM + 1) reproduces it for any cell; how it was counted is not documented.
The MERFISH data of Fig. 5B are not in the dandiset and the paper gives no public location for them.

paper_notes.statement: The paper's metadata table (LeeDalley_manuscript_metadata_v2.csv) repeats one row (specimen 819133824, a culture microglial cell), giving 779 rows for 778 cells, so a count over its rows gives 181 culture microglial cells where metaPatch, stored with the transcriptomes, has 180. With the repeated row removed, the condition2 calls of the two tables agree for all 778 cells.

19 of the paper's 84 electrophysiology features (width_suprathresh, postap_slope, sag_area, sag_peak_t, sag_tau, the depolarizing sag features, ahp_delay_ratio, trough_slowdeltav and adp_v_last) are computed by code the paper says "will be released in a future version of IPFX"; public IPFX 2.1.2 does not compute them, so counts over 84 features (43 of 84 differ between acute and culture) cannot be repeated. The definitions of the adaptation ratios and of the mean and maximum ISI summaries are not given precisely enough to match the paper's table (isi_adapt_ratio agrees for 27% of cells).

Which sweep stands for the interspike interval and AP width in Fig. 1L is not given. With the rheobase-sweep ISI, the ISI differs between acute and culture PVALB WFDC2 cells (FDR p = 0.016), and with the hero-sweep ISI it does not (0.75). Could the authors say which sweeps Fig. 1L and fig. S2C use?

The code's gene filter for the ion-channel and morphology-type gene analyses (keepGenes) is built from dissociated-nuclei data (complete_facs_data_sets.RData) and sex and mitochondrial gene lists that the repository does not hold, so figs. S2D (7 of 114 channel genes) and the 253 genes of Fig. 4D cannot be repeated from the repository.
In the code's ion-channel analysis, apply(lm_pval, 2, p.adjust) adjusts each gene's three term p-values with Holm, not across genes, and its comment calls this FDR correction.

Whether the SST population of Fig. 5D (morphology UMAP) includes the SST FRZB neurons, which the paper moves to the PVALB subclass for subclass-level analyses, is not said. The DBC clustering test passes in the UMAP with them (subclass_label) and fails without them (Revised_subclass_label). Could the authors say which cells the panel shows?

Which sweep's average firing rate fig. S8B compares between species is not given. With the rate at rheobase + 40 pA, the Sst 5 rates do not differ between human and mouse, and with the rate at rheobase they do (FDR p 7.3e-04). Could the authors say which sweep they used?

The paper reports 75 LAMP5/PAX6, 99 VIP, 149 SST and 352 PVALB neurons with electrophysiology. Its own metadata table gives 67, 111, 156 and 370 for the rows with Has_ephys under the revised subclasses, and 675 cells with a rheobase here split 63, 99, 155 and 358, so the selection behind the paper's counts is not documented.

The paper's own microglial calls (condition2 of the metadata table) call 0.418 of acute and 0.385 of culture cells microglial. The Results say the signature was observed in a subset of acute neurons "although the effect was less pronounced"; by the fraction of cells it is not less frequent in acute cells, while the mean expression of the 269 signature genes in the called cells is lower (3.8 against 5.9).

entries.title: Resonance of human and mouse cortical interneurons (Shamugia et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Shamugia, Weiler, ... Goriounova and Mansvelder (2026) on human cortical interneuron resonance on dandiset 000630 (210 human layer 1 interneurons, Chartrand et al. 2023), with dandiset 000636 (human acute and slice-culture interneurons, Lee, Dalley et al. 2023) and the paper's mouse cells in dandiset 000020 (Gouwens et al. 2020). The notebook computes impedance profiles, resonance frequency and strength, sag ratio and input resistance, and tests how they differ between species, preparations, regions and diseases, how they relate, and how they relate to ion channel gene expression. The depth, ZD7288, Allen Brain Map and modelling findings are not tested.
